s: The purpose of the proverbs: the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Wisdom calls out in the streets.
Seeking wisdom protects you from evil ways.
Trust in the Lord with all your heart. Wisdom is more precious than riches.
A father urges his sons to get wisdom above all things.
A warning against the adulterous woman, and the joy of faithfulness in marriage.
Warnings about rash promises, laziness, troublemakers and adultery.
A young man is led astray by a seductive woman.
Wisdom speaks: she was with God at the creation of the world.
Wisdom and folly each invite people to their house.
Proverbs of Solomon: the just and the wicked contrasted.
Honesty, generosity and humility bring blessing.
The value of discipline, truthful speech and diligent work.
Wisdom, hope and the company we keep.
The wise and foolish in the home and in speech.
A gentle answer turns away wrath. The Lord sees everything.
People make plans, but the Lord directs their steps. Pride goes before a fall.
Peace, friendship and controlling one's words.
The power of the tongue and the worth of a true friend.
Poverty with integrity, kindness to the poor, and discipline of children.
Warnings about wine, laziness and dishonesty.
The Lord weighs the heart. Doing justice is better than sacrifice.
A good name is better than riches. Train a child in the way he should go. Sayings of the wise begin.
Sayings on self-control, greed and listening to parents.
Do not envy the wicked. Wisdom builds a house.
More proverbs of Solomon, collected by Hezekiah's men: humility and self-control.
Sayings about fools, sluggards and gossips.
Do not boast about tomorrow. Faithful are the wounds of a friend.
The just are bold as a lion. Honesty and fairness.
Correction, justice and the fear of man.
The sayings of Agur: God's word is pure. Things too wonderful to know.
The words of King Lemuel's mother, and the praise of a worthy wife.

11: “Solicitous” here means anxious, full of worry.
In older English “corn” meant any grain, such as wheat or barley.
12: the bowels of the wicked are cruel
The bowels were thought of as the seat of feeling. Here: the heart, deep compassion.

18: the inner parts of the bowels
